column1: # Places the catalogue folded into one function by their fingerprint although they are other code
# (program.py read_split_places): each variant gets its places as its own name, and calls to the
# function are resolved through the caller's own jal (lower.py).
# The level font width wrapper: in the story levels func_L01_00412E50 calls func_L01_00412618, which
# hands back a float in $f0; in the multiplayer maps the same wrapper calls another routine
# (level 39's 0x00519EB8), whose result their callers read in $v0 (func_L39_004B9218 tests it
# (The class type getters, the loading flight's destination and the other 8-byte leaves the catalogue used to
# file one row along are filed by their callers' call sites since rac3-decomp 7453660c: no split needed.)
# Folded one-call wrappers whose copies call other callees by level (port/tools/hostgen/variant_callees.py):
# each level's copy is the wrapper of the callee its own jal reaches, so the places that reach another
# callee than the Veldin copy's go to a variant of their own, with that callee's result and arguments.
# A list adder of the same instructions as the draw callback adder func_L01_00404A10 (a pair to the
# lists at its own globals, a count of at most 0x40), but its own lists: in levels 3, 11, 16 and 23
# the catalogue put this other routine in func_L01_00404A10's row, where the level's own copy of
# the adder sits 0x50 before func_L01_00404A60 (level 23's 0x003E7A98, lists 0x001E7680/0x001E7780)
# and this one far off (0x0043A540, lists 0x001EDE68/0x001EDF68). Level 23's mobys hand it
# (moby, 3); translated as the adder, they went into the draw callbacks, and DrawFrame
# (func_L01_00404A60) called each moby's address as a function.
# The same four levels lay their callback lists out otherwise: Veldin's adder of the third list
# (func_L01_004048D0, 0x50 before its runner func_L01_00404920) has no copy there, and the catalogue
# put in its row the adder of the second list instead (level 16's 0x00414C20, lists
# 0x001E87C0/0x001E88C0, 0x50 before the second list's runner 0x00414C70). Translated as the third
# list's adder, each callback the level added to the second list went into the third list's count
# with the second's tables: DrawFrame's third runner (func_L01_00404920) called empty entries, a call
# to 0 a tick (levels 16 and 23), and the second list lost its callbacks.
# The places above whose catalogue row is another function's are, by the callers' own jals, copies of
# func_L01_00412E50 and func_L01_00412E30 (each the next row's wrapper, the same callee's twin):
# hostgen.json "more_places" names them so, where no other Veldin name holds them, so the calls by
# Veldin's address (OPENRAC_LCODE: the movie mode's func_L01_004B88B0 every frame, a text layout's
# width wrapper) reach the level's own copy. Without a copy the address was paired by the
# The front end's func_0039BD90 (a wrapper of func_0039BD08 handing on $a0-$a2) has its copies in
# every level under that name, and the executable has another function at 0x0039BD90 (the menu flags
# from the saved state, matched C since rac3-decomp 7fc8c2c0, void with no arguments). With the
# executable's C the name took no arguments and the level copies handed none on; the copies are
# The byte getters and the clear in front of the Vid-comic password panel (8-byte leaves: jr $ra;
# lbu $v0 / sb $zero, off($gp)): the catalogue folds them by fingerprint and, in the Phoenix (03) and
# the Insomniac Museum (24), the two levels with the panel (func_L03_003A3838, "Enter Password",
# text 0x18C2), puts the panel's own getter and clear (0x00482B80, 0x00482B88: its entry flag, Veldin's
# gp-0x37DC) in the rows of func_L01_004CB548 and func_L01_004DB2E8, and func_L01_004CB548's real twin
# (0x004B8F30, the flag func_L01_004CB540 sets: the help box and HUD set it every few frames) in the
# row of func_L01_004D8928. Paired by those rows, Veldin's flag 0x001DB084 had two places on the
# Phoenix, the panel read the help box's flag and opened on every arrival ("Enter Password" over the
# corridor). The panel's leaves are their own functions; the real twins are their rows' places
# The help box's flag setter in Holostar Studios as Clank (23): the catalogue folds the 8-byte $gp
# byte stores by fingerprint and puts another flag's setter (0x0045CCE8: sb $a0, -0x483A($gp), read by
# func_L01_0047B388's and func_L01_0047B5B0's copies) in the row of func_L01_004CB540, and
# func_L01_004CB540's real twin (0x004ACE68: sb $a0, -0x186C($gp), the byte the getter func_L01_004CB548
# at 0x004ACE70 reads) in the row of func_L01_004D8820. Paired by those rows, Veldin's flag 0x001DB084
# went to 0x001D8076 there: the help box's setter wrote the other flag. As the Phoenix's rows above;
# the real twin is its row's place (hostgen.json "more_places").
